title: Piano in dance bands and Edward Wright
summary: Pope's bands always had piano; his pianist Edward Wright became an arranger in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: In the old days for the dance bands, when you first had a small group for the dance bands, did they always use piano or did sometime you play without a piano? Well we very suddenly played without a piano. Because in New Orleans a lot of the bands just used... they didn't have a... Yes sir. A lot of the little taverns and basses they still don't have a piano so they'll play without just using guitar and bass. I wondered if they did that much here.

Well we played with the piano most of the time. Always had a piano playing. In fact, I had one of the best piano players I believe... well... I don't know what he... he composed some music and he was an arranger for some concern in Chicago.

American Conservancy. Who's that? American Conservancy. Oh the American... I was in Chicago. I knew that. Edward Wright. Edward Wright. Yeah, he was Edward Wright. He's still there. He's in a cast now. Edward Wright. Uh-huh. Edward Wright. He's very interested to talk to him. He's in a cast. He was run old for years... about a couple of years ago.
